**Built and PROVEN against production 2026-07-31** (`db27609`). `POST /api/kira/chat/text`.

## Why it is not a fallback

Two reasons and only one is the microphone. The commonest cause of "no mic" is an owner clicking
**Block** on the permission prompt — likely, not exotic, for a man who has told nobody he is selling.
And he has asked for typing in his own words four separate times: he cannot paste a URL or a message,
only upload a file. See [[project-kira-captured-asks]] if it exists, else `docs/CAPTURED_ASKS.md`.

## The design decisions worth keeping

- **ONE persona, two transports.** The system prompt is **read from the deployed ElevenLabs agent**,
  not rebuilt locally. A locally-assembled persona drifts the first time either side is edited, and
  the symptom is her being subtly different depending on how you spoke to her. Reading the live
  prompt also inherits every patch applied to running agents that never went through the repo.
- **It writes to the SAME memory.** Turns land in `conversations` / `conversation_messages` with a
  `text:<uuid>` conversation id, so a typed session stays distinguishable in Genome provenance.
  Distil runs on `pagehide` via `sendBeacon` — the text equivalent of the post-call webhook. Without
  it, everything typed stays a transcript and never becomes Genome.
- **Four refusals**: won't answer at all if the live prompt can't be read (replying as a generic
  assistant in Kira's window is the worst outcome available) · a failed model call does NOT persist
  his message (a turn stored with no answer resurfaces as something she ignored) · the insert is
  awaited, never floated · errors render into the transcript rather than being swallowed.

## Verified, not assumed

Driven against production with a real QA session (minted via
`cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs --magic-link`): unauthenticated **401** · real message
**200** answering as Kira · **continuity PASS** (told her a gate code, she returned it next turn) ·
4 messages persisted · empty **400** · over-length **413** · unknown agent **404** · distil on end
**`{"ok":true,"distilled":true}`** · and the fact reached `kira_memory` as
*"The gate code at Lot 91 is 4417."*

## The bug that produced it — worth not repeating

`textInput` was first switched on as a one-prop "fix" without reading the widget. `submitText` sends
to the live session when connected and otherwise calls `props.onTextFallbackSubmit?.(value)` — an
optional call on a prop nobody passed. With no mic there is no session, so typing cleared the box and
did nothing: no message, no reply, no error, no console output. **Worse than the honest "Not
supported" it replaced**, sitting on the one action the product exists for.

⚠️ **Note the two paths are different.** With a WORKING mic and a live call, typed text goes via
`convo.sendUserMessage()` into ElevenLabs — it does reach the transcript as a user turn, and the
agent used to deny seeing it (fixed by the typed-input prompt section, live on all 11 agents).
`onTextFallbackSubmit` only fires when there is NO live session.

**QA gotcha:** `kira_agents.user_id` is the APP user id; a minted session carries the AUTH id. Bridge
through `users.auth_user_id` or the ownership check 404s.

**2026-08-05/06: the big go-live sprint.** 12 commits to main, Stripe moved to live keys,
four client-reported bugs diagnosed. Karen answered almost every open decision in one meeting.

## Shipped to main (all deployed)

`ed38f9c`+mkt fabricated social proof REMOVED from live site · `420b263` create-project errors visible ·
`6f38393`+mkt social-proof shell (empty, flag-gated) · `27549b4`+mkt#3 CTA switch merged (inert) ·

`7e8be92`+mkt CTA label "Get started" · `da13b8e` terms payment/renewal/cancellation + version
re-acceptance · `d710824` cancellation path · `8076e5e` terms gate blocking made visible ·
`fe0149d` /signup reachable when signed in.

## ⚠️ Stripe is LIVE in production (from 2026-08-05)

Keys + all 6 price IDs live; **preview deliberately left on TEST keys** — they used to share one
env row spanning `preview+production`, so going live would have put every preview on live keys.
Split first (see [[reference_mmcbuild_vercel_github_topology]]).

**Traps hit:** (1) the price IDs Dennis first supplied were the TEST set; the ones in the keys file
were all `prod_…` **PRODUCT** ids — checkout needs `price_…`. **Resolve live prices from the Stripe
API with the live key** rather than transcribing (`GET /v1/prices?active=true&expand[]=data.product`),
which settles mode and accuracy at once. (2) **`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is still unproven** — test and
live signing secrets both start `whsec_`, so a mismatch is invisible: payment succeeds, subscription
silently never activates. Only a real card proves it (SCRUM-332).

⚠️ **Live Stripe portal has ZERO billing_portal configurations** → cancellation via the portal may
fail for the first real customer. Unproven (no live customer to test). Fix: Stripe Dashboard →
Settings → Billing → Customer portal → enable "Cancel subscriptions".

## Diagnostic techniques worth reusing

- **Click does nothing → find the overlay.** `document.elementFromPoint(cx,cy)` at the element's
  centre. Karen's "can't change state region" was the terms-gate `fixed inset-0 z-[100]` backdrop
  eating every click while the form stayed legible behind it at 60% opacity. The checkboxes were fine.
- **"It won't let me sign up" → check for a redirect, not a bug.** `curl -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url}"` with and without a session cookie. `/signup` 307'd to `/dashboard` for signed-in users.
- **Mint a real session to reproduce**: `cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs --magic-link`
  with `QA_TEST_EMAIL`, then `curl -b` or feed the cookie to `/browse`.
- **Vercel `sensitive` env vars are write-only** — even `?decrypt=true` returns nothing. Use
  `updatedAt` timestamps to tell whether a value was actually changed.

## Standing rules learned

- **Vercel tokens are scoped AT CREATION to one team.** A token made for the decoy team can never
  see the live one, and the diff it produces looks perfectly valid. Always verify the project id
  (`prj_mNQT2kY6CqcTeiZhJMX1VqE5qB9f` = live app) before trusting any Vercel answer.
- **A `throw` in a server action is invisible in production** — see
  [[project_ai_router_and_honest_error_standards]]. Return `{ error }`.
- **Terms versioning**: `TERMS_VERSION` was written but never read, so bumping it re-prompted nobody.
  Fixed in `lib/legal/terms.ts`; the bump re-prompts all 43 profiles.

exist, **the real-card test (332)**. PRs #148+mkt#4 (attribution) unblocked and ready to merge.
Not done: privacy-policy disclosure draft, case-studies links, enterprise-enquiry ticket.

**Pipeline is NOT special** — it's the first member of the "HAND-BUILT product" category. Every product needs the same 14 survey `data-*` markers; what differs is who plants them: a factory-GENERATED product gets them from the build (markerProps); a hand-built/pre-existing product has no generator and can't be safely regenerated (the generative design→build would rewrite the real app), so its markers are **wired manually** = the "marker-pass." Every pre-built product the operator onboards hits this.

## The marker-pass mechanism (shipped 2026-06-17, commit c2e8ed5)
- `src/lib/methodology/spec-marker-attrs.ts` — `specMarkerAttrs(cardRow)` maps a product_validation_status row → `{ "data-promise": …, … }` (the 14 SURVEY_MARKERS fields + `data-why-now` from `feasibility.why_now`). ONE source of truth.
- `<SpecMarkers slug/>` (`src/components/pipeline/SpecMarkers.tsx`) — server component, reads the card via cockpitDb, emits a hidden `<div hidden {...attrs}/>`. For products co-located on the pipeline instance (pipeline itself). Used on `/pipeline/welcome` (slug=pipeline).
- `GET /api/public/spec-markers/[slug]` — PUBLIC endpoint (outside the middleware matcher) returning any product's marker attrs. **The foundation for EXTERNAL pre-built products** (separate codebases, no pipeline-DB access): their shared drop-in fetches this and SSRs the attrs (the survey reads server HTML, NO JS exec — markers must be server-rendered).
- `public/survey-manifest.json` → `{"routes":["/pipeline/welcome"]}`. The survey fetches `<mvp_url>/survey-manifest.json`, gets routes (∪ `/`), fetches each, greps markers. No manifest → falls back to `/`.
- Verified live: manifest ✅, 14/14 spec markers SSR'd on /welcome ✅, endpoint ✅.

## ⚠️ THE why_now/P3 GOTCHA (bites every pre-built product)
PRE-HARD **P3 = distributor + distributor_outcomes + data-why-now**, and P1/P2/P3 GATE the RENOVATION verdict (P4 is informational, not gating). The coach often fills the 14 graded spec fields but leaves **`feasibility.why_now = null`** (it did for pipeline) → no `data-why-now` marker → **P3 fails → TEARDOWN despite 14/14 evidenced.** Fix: populate the card's `feasibility.why_now` (product content — the "why now"). Then `<SpecMarkers>` emits it automatically. **Rollout implication: ensure the coach captures why_now, or P3 fails for every pre-built product.**

## ⚠️ TWO MORE GOTCHAS (found running pipeline's own survey, 2026-06-17 — bite every pre-built product)
1. **Root must be FETCH-FOLLOWABLE to 200 (P1).** The survey reads the mvp_url ROOT for P1 (homepage 200), and node `fetch` (no JS) must reach 200. Pipeline's `app/page.tsx` used React `redirect('/pipeline/welcome')`, which served a **header-less 307** → `fetch` got `status 307, ok:false, redirected:false` → P1 fail → verdict **UNREADABLE** (no score) despite a clean /welcome. Fix: redirect via **next.config `redirects()`** (proper Location header, fetch follows) — commit 45ef4e3. Now root → 200 (redirected→/pipeline/welcome). Any pre-built product whose root redirects via a client/React redirect (or a header-less 307) will UNREADABLE the same way — use a config/HTTP redirect, or have the root answer 200.
2. **icp_stage is an ENUM marker** (`seed|growth|scale|operating-business|enterprise`) — the only ENUM of the 14. The card stores PROSE → off-enum → not evidenced → 13/14 (still clears MIN_EVIDENCED ≥12/14, so it didn't block pipeline's RENOVATION). **FIXED in the coach (commit 33bb36a):** `ICP_STAGE_VALUES` in apply-coach-fields.ts; the graded path normalises + enum-validates icp_stage (CoachFieldError lists valid tokens); VOICE_PREAMBLE tells Morgan icp_stage/demand_tier/distributor_benefit_mode take a TOKEN not prose, and why_now is REQUIRED. Pipeline's card icp_stage set to `operating-business` for a clean 14/14 on the next run.

## PIPELINE SURVEY = RENOVATION (2026-06-17) — survey gate passed
After the root-redirect fix (45ef4e3), pipeline's survey verdicted **RENOVATION** (13/14, PRE-HARD pass). Card notes seen: "Unbound — no validation tied to a deployment yet" (the user-side Run survey posts deployment_id=null, so the verdict isn't deployment-pinned — informational), and "Readiness HARD gate not passed (5/7)" — that's the SEPARATE Gate-1 readiness gate, NOT the survey: #39 (no secrets) + #40 (Vercel env) are "not yet tested" (+ 9 other unscored). Next step for pipeline: **"Run full validation"** to record those → HARD gate → weighted score. (Survey = Stage 3 / "build evidences spec"; readiness = Stage 5 / go-live gate.)

## VOICE: the canonical shape + the auditor false-negative (resolved 2026-06-17)
- **Canonical voice = the COACH (intake) + the INTERVIEW agent**, both with BAKED agent ids in `voice.config.ts` (COACH_AGENT_ID default `agent_1601kv24fz3efvfb8yyhe5rjazw6`, provisioned for pipeline; works with NO Vercel env). The Morgan intake coach IS live (operator-confirmed) — reachable via "New idea" → /pipeline/new-ideas.
- **The floating "cockpit clarifier" was LEGACY** (corporate-ai-solutions carryover), read `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_COCKPIT_CLARIFIER` (never provisioned → rendered null), NOT the canonical shape. **REMOVED** (pipeline e3a295a + 7713b6b: PipelineChromeClarifier/AdminChromeClarifier/CockpitClarifier + clarifier-context + the voice.config consts). The PipelineChromeClarifier I'd added to "fix §6" was the same legacy widget — mistaken; reverted.
- **#10 was a FALSE-NEGATIVE** → recorded pass (judge override): the coach is the voice; the auditor (a) read STALE cred env names → login silently failed → saw only the public landing, and (b) hunted the legacy clarifier. **Fixed the voice-auditor** (cais-shared-services 46ef2ed): reads canonical `QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL/PASSWORD` first, and after login visits the `--voice-url` surface AUTHED (the coach is behind auth + not the authed root).
- **REMAINING (orchestration):** the validation-run dispatch (pipeline run-full-validation → validation-run.yml → voice-auditor args) should pass **`--voice-url=/pipeline/new-ideas`** (the coach surface) so the auditor auto-lands on it. Until then #10 stands on the judge override.
- **#40 was a FALSE-`na`** (CI can't reach Vercel) → recorded pass: Vercel API verified 34/34 env vars sensitive, 0 development, 0 plaintext. The portfolio fix to stop the recurring `na`: give the validation-run CI a Vercel token so the auto-probe can verify env.

## REMAINING C — DONE (2026-06-17): `@caistech/spec-markers@0.1.0` published
Built + published (cais-shared-services commit `3e5acca`, tag `v0.1.38`, on GitHub Packages). It's a
thin async-Server-Component drop-in: `<SpecMarkers slug="x" pipelineUrl?/>` fetches the public
`GET <pipeline>/api/public/spec-markers/<slug>` (default base `https://pipeline-nine-silk.vercel.app`,
override via prop or `SPEC_MARKERS_ENDPOINT`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_PIPELINE_URL`) and SSRs the attrs;
degrade-don't-break (returns null/{} on failure). Also `fetchSpecMarkers(slug, opts)` + `buildSurveyManifest(routes)`.
The marker MAPPING stays single-sourced in pipeline (the endpoint builds `{attrs}`), so the package
never drifts. Verified live: 15 attrs incl. `data-why-now`. **Per external pre-built product:** install
`@caistech/spec-markers`, drop `<SpecMarkers slug="x"/>` on the public landing (a SERVER component),
write `public/survey-manifest.json` (`buildSurveyManifest(['/'])`), set the card `mvp_url`, and ensure
`feasibility.why_now` is set (else P3 fails). Cataloged in SHARED_SERVICES.md. See
[[project_validation_agent_surface_resolution]] for the companion #40/agent fixes.

Four scripting gotchas that each cost a retry while landing the 2026-06-18 middleware
fix + Vercel infra fixes (Windows 11, git-bash, `python` = Windows `C:\Program Files\Python312`):

1. **`/tmp` write-vs-read mismatch (Windows-python ↔ git-bash-curl).** Writing a request
   body with `python -c "open('/tmp/x','w')..."` then `curl --data @/tmp/x` **fails**
   (`curl: --data: error encountered when reading a file`) — Windows python resolves
   `/tmp/x` to a different real path than git-bash/curl do. **Fix:** use a **cwd-relative**
   file (e.g. `vresp.json` in the cwd, which both resolve identically) or pass the body
   **inline** `--data "$body"`. Same family as the MSYS path-mangling note in
   [[reference_auth_email_token_hash_canon]].

2. **`UID` is a readonly bash builtin.** `UID=$(curl ... )` silently fails with
   `UID: readonly variable` and `$UID` then expands to the OS user id, so the next call
   hits a garbage URL. Name the var anything else (`DEP`, `dpl`, …). Same caution for other
   builtins (`PWD`, `PPID`, `EUID`).

3. **Vercel pre-commit hooks fail inside a fresh `git worktree`.** A worktree shares `.git`
   but **not** `node_modules`, so a husky pre-commit that runs `tsc`/`next lint` errors with
   `Cannot find module 'next/server'` on every file — a deps-less-environment artifact, not a
   real type error. For a trivial, proven change (e.g. the middleware 2-line edit) commit with
   `git commit --no-verify`; the real typecheck still runs in Vercel/CI. (Hit on
   corporate-ai-solutions.)

4. **Fixing a registry-token 401 can UNMASK a second, pre-existing build error.** After
   setting the missing `@caistech` GitHub-Packages token on Longtail's Vercel project (the
   [[reference_caistech_vercel_registry_token]] gotcha), `install` passed but `next build`
   then failed on a *separate* pre-existing issue: `.eslintrc.json` enabled
   `react-compiler/react-compiler` with **no `eslint-plugin-react-compiler` installed** →
   "Definition for rule not found" hard-fails the build regardless of the rule's "warn"
   severity. The 401 had been failing first and hiding it. **Lesson:** after an infra/deploy
   unblock, re-pull the build logs — a green install ≠ a green deploy; expect to peel a
   second layer. Fix there was to delete the orphaned rule line.

Reusable landing pattern proven this session: to push an isolated hotfix to `main` from a
repo sitting on a **feature branch with unrelated WIP**, add a `git worktree` off
`origin/main`, apply + commit only the fix there, push + PR, then `worktree remove` and
`git checkout -- <file>` to restore the feature tree — the WIP is never touched.

**Measured three times on 2026-07-31.** Writing code through `python - <<'EOF'` heredocs corrupts
backslash escapes, silently.

The worst instance: `/\bthe (user|agent|assistant)\b/i` was written into `lib/kira/welcome-back.ts`
with the `\b` collapsed into a **literal backspace byte (0x08)**. The source *looked* correct in every
editor and grep view. The regex matched nothing. It took four test runs to find, because the code read
right.

Two lesser instances the same day: a `\'` that became a no-op replace in a Drive query escape, and
`\\s` surviving only because `\s` is not a valid Python escape.

**Why:** valid Python escapes (`\b` `\n` `\t` `\r` `\f` `\v` `\a` `\0`) are interpreted before the
file is written; `\s` `\d` `\w` survive by accident because Python does not recognise them. So the
dangerous ones are exactly the ones that look most innocuous.

**How to apply:**

- **Prefer the `Write` / `Edit` tools** for any file containing a regex or an escape. They do not pass
  through a shell.
- If a heredoc is unavoidable, build the escape from char codes rather than typing it:
  `String.fromCharCode(92)` for a backslash, or in Python `chr(92) + 'b'`.
- **Scan after writing:** a file containing 0x08 is always a bug —
  `python -c "import sys;s=open(F,encoding='utf-8').read();print(s.count(chr(8)))"`.
- **Test the behaviour, not the presence.** A test asserting the guard's *effect* catches this in one
  run; reading the source never does. This is the same lesson as
  [[feedback-grade-capability-not-function-name]], arriving from the other direction.

**The generalisation worth keeping:** this is the same failure class the whole Kira session was spent
fixing in other people's code — `void mirrorTask` that looked like a write, `classifyOne` returning
'none' under a comment saying it did the opposite, a text box wired to a prop nobody passed. A guard
that exists, reads well and does nothing. I introduced it twice in one file within an hour of
documenting it.

**2026-08-01, three instances in one session.** Each had been written correctly, committed, and
recorded as fixed. All three were still broken in production, and in every case the *edit* was fine
— something downstream of it silently won.

**Why:** a diff proves what you wrote, not what the user gets. All three would have been caught by
one observation of the running product and none by re-reading the code — which is exactly why they
survived a re-read.

## The three

1. **CSS lost on source order.** `app/globals.css` overrode the convai widget's mobile rule with a
   bare `.convai-panel--embedded` — specificity (0,1,0), **identical** to the package's
   `.convai-panel`. Equal specificity is settled by source order, and the package **injects its
   stylesheet at runtime as an inline `<style>`**, so it always lands after the bundled `<link>` and
   always wins. The override was **inert from the day it shipped** (2026-07-27) and the same 375px
   overflow was found again four days later. Fix: double the class to
   `.convai-panel.convai-panel--embedded` → (0,2,0), which no injection order can overturn.
   **Whenever you override a package that injects CSS at runtime, out-specify it — do not out-order
   it.**
2. **A link nobody recognised as a link.** The `/admin/login` reject banner had carried "sign in as a
   user" since 2026-07-20, and a tester still reported there was no way back. It was `font-semibold
   underline` in `text-amber-800` — **the same colour as the sentence containing it** — so it read as
   emphasis. *A link a user does not recognise as a link is, to that user, not a link.* Now a
   bordered button, own line, 44px target.
3. **A config describing a product Kira stopped being.** `agent-readiness.config.ts` still sold "a
   patient, knowledgeable AI companion who guides you through learning new skills" and pointed at
   `/create-kira` + `/personal-journey`. It is the **only** thing AI search and browser agents read
   to decide what Kira is (drives `/llms.txt`, landing JSON-LD, `/.well-known/agent.json`) — so
   agents described the wrong product entirely, to the channel most likely to arrive that way.

## How to apply

- **Close a fix by observing the effect in the running product**, at the viewport/identity/state the
  report described. "The code says X" is not evidence that X reaches anyone.
- **A finding from a human tester that contradicts the code is usually a real finding about
  perception**, not a mistaken tester. Ask what they saw, not whether the element exists.
- Beware anything whose effect depends on **order, specificity, injection timing, or locale**: those
  are the classes that read correct and behave wrong. (A bare `toLocaleDateString()` in a server
  component takes the *server's* locale — en-US on Vercel — which is the same shape of bug.)
- Escapes through shell heredocs corrupt regexes the same way — see
  [[feedback-escapes-mangled-through-tooling]].

Related: [[project-kira-naive-tester-state]], [[feedback-no-complete-headline-over-a-caveat]].

Found in production. The 08:03 conversation is summarised as "sending a test
email, which the agent successfully drafted and dispatched." The task is sitting
in the orchestrator right now, status `queued`, undrafted and unsent, and the
recipient it captured was mcdennis@gmail.com — a voice transcription that dropped
a letter from the owner's own address, so even a successful send would have gone
to a stranger.

ROOT CAUSE. askModel swallows every failure and returns null, so a 429, a timeout
and a malformed completion are indistinguishable from "nothing to draft".
draftForIntent then returns null, and /v1/dispatch treated that identically to a
background job awaiting its turn: the row went in as `queued` and the caller was
answered "Accepted." Kira read that back as success. Being told a thing happened
when it did not is worse than being told it cannot happen at all — the owner acts
on it, and finds out from his client.

A spoken request the classifier RECOGNISED but the drafter could not produce is
now `failed`, carries result.error='draft_failed', and answers with something Kira
can say out loud: nothing has been sent.

Kira now reports the outcome rather than inferring it. approve_task returns
explicit `sent` and `failed` alongside `done`, and the agents are told to read the
result instead of assuming it — "accepted", "queued" and "noted" are not "sent".

THE BUILD QUEUE WAS READING THE WRONG DATABASE. /admin/asked-for and the alert,
shipped an hour earlier, both read kira_tasks — but with KIRA_SWARM_ADAPTER live,
dispatch goes to the orchestrator's own Supabase project. The page would have sat
showing this morning's stale rows while real requests arrived somewhere it never
looks, which reads as "nobody is asking for anything" — the worst possible failure
for a queue whose only job is to tell you what to build. Undone dispatches are now
mirrored into kira_tasks whichever brain handled them, and the alert fires on
`failed` as well as `unsupported`, since `failed` is exactly what this bug produces.

AND THE PATCH SCRIPT WAS APPENDING, NOT REPLACING. Its dedupe logic was correct
and unused: the PATCH body still sent `current + boundary` while `next` sat
computed two lines above, so every run stacked another copy of the section onto
the same prompt — four deep on one agent before anyone counted. The read-back
checked only that the marker was PRESENT, which cannot see this failure because it
is present four times. It now asserts exactly one, and collapsed the fleet back to
one copy on the next run.

match landed, guarded by a single assertion that the file changed at all.

   the call rather than happening during it. get_conversation_context had the
   same defect on both its id params.

   uid identity is unchanged and is not an alternative to this: uid answers
   "whose memory", the platform-filled conversation id answers "which
   conversation", and save_message needs the second one.

2. reminder was the one kind the product could not keep its promise on. The
   owner said "remind me tomorrow", the classifier captured a free-text due_hint
   that nothing ever parsed, approval marked the row done, and Kira said "Done."
   Nothing fired, then or ever, because nothing swept the table.

   The classifier now resolves the spoken time to an absolute timestamp against
   a stated current time; approval moves the row to 'scheduled' with a due_at
   rather than claiming completion; and an hourly sweep delivers it. A reminder
   with no resolvable time now fails honestly at approval instead of being
   accepted and silently never firing.

   Idempotent by status — the sweep reads only 'scheduled' rows and flips each to
   'done' on success, so a re-run cannot double-send, and a delivery failure
   stays scheduled to retry rather than burning the reminder.

history drift, so never a blind db push).

KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: there is no per-owner timezone — users
carries no timezone column — so relative times resolve against a portfolio
default (KIRA_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE, Australia/Perth). An owner in Sydney saying
"9am" currently gets 9am Perth. The timezone used is recorded on the task
artifact so a wrong reminder is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

* fix(reminders): give the owner a timezone, and stop the script reverting the tool fix

Closes the limitation the previous commit declared rather than leaving it as a
note. users.timezone is nullable on purpose: a default would be a guess wearing
the costume of a fact, silently giving every existing owner 'Australia/Perth'
with no way to tell a confirmed zone from an assumed one. NULL means "not
captured", the caller falls back to KIRA_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE explicitly, and a
later capture is an improvement rather than an overwrite. IANA names only —
an offset cannot survive daylight saving, which is exactly when a reminder
would silently drift by an hour.

The zone is recorded on the task artifact and the spoken readback reads it back
from there rather than from the current default, so a readback always describes

is captured or corrected afterwards.

fix(portfolio-gate): first-paint reported PASS having verified nothing

Two defects found by running the check against real deployments rather than by
reasoning about it. The first is the serious one.

1. NOT MEASURED read as PASSED.

Non-200 routes were skipped on the grounds that reachability is public-routes'
verdict — which is true, and which silently produced a green tick over a Vercel
preview whose deployment protection redirected all ELEVEN marked routes to an SSO
wall: 0 findings, exit 0, nothing whatsoever verified.

That is precisely the failure this package documents in three other files and
exists to end, reintroduced here on the first run of the newest check. It is worth
stating plainly because of how it happened: the trap was read, understood, quoted
while writing the file, and then walked into anyway, because "defer to the other
audit" and "check nothing" look identical in code and only diverge in the result.

An unmeasurable route is now a warning, and the audit FAILS outright when none
could be measured, naming the protection wall as the usual cause. A green tick
must never be available to a run that established nothing.

2. Hex character references inflated every measurement.

The entity decoder handled `'` but not `'`, and Next.js emits the hex
form — so "what's" counted as eleven visible characters instead of six, on
any page containing an apostrophe, which is most of them. Both forms now decode.

Verified against Kira production across the fix that motivated the check:
/plan 16 -> 300 characters of content, /login 16 -> 49, and /login passes on the
heading signal rather than the character count, which is the case the
text-OR-heading disjunction was written for.

Two operational facts about the **property-services** engine (edge functions at ref
`qppddipgixhinprliyxh`), learned live 2026-07-05. Related: [[project_canonical_property_feed_enforcement]].

**1. A code deploy does NOT refresh the `/derive` cache — evict to roll a fix out.**
`/derive` (`supabase/functions/derive/index.ts`) caches every result in the **`property_lookups`**
table, keyed by **`address_normalised`** = `normaliseAddress(address)` (lowercased, punctuation
stripped — e.g. `1 london circuit canberra act 2600`). On a request it does
`.eq("address_normalised", normalised)` and, if a row with a `profile` exists, **returns that stored
profile verbatim** (sets `metadata.cached=true`, fires `increment_lookup_hit`) and runs NO derivation.
Only a cache MISS runs the real logic + upserts (`onConflict: "address_normalised"`).
→ `supabase functions deploy derive` changes the CODE; the cache is DATA. A bug fix is **invisible for
any already-derived address** until its row is evicted or overwritten. Proven this session: after
deploying the LGA fix, `1 London Circuit` STILL returned the old wrong value until I
`DELETE FROM property_lookups WHERE address_normalised ILIKE '%london circuit%'` and re-derived.
**Rules:** to VERIFY an engine fix, test a never-cached address OR delete the test row first; to ROLL A
DATA-CORRECTING FIX to existing users, **sweep the cache** (evict every now-wrong row) or they keep the
old value. Treat the cache as serve-until-evicted (observed stale served with no TTL refresh, despite a
`metadata.expiresAt`). "Green deploy ≠ users see the fix" — the metered cache sits in front of the engine.
Evict/sweep via the Management API (node `fetch`, `~/.supabase-token` sbp_, not curl-execFileSync on Windows).

**2. The LGA fuzzy name-matcher MUST be state-scoped (the ACT→Gold Coast bug).**
`resolveLGACode(name, state)` (`_shared/lga-resolve.ts`) maps a council NAME (Mapbox reverse-geocode
`text`, or a state portal) to an `lga_plans` row by fuzzy matching across all ~547 LGAs nationally, in
tiers: exact → partial substring (either direction) → keyword. BUG: tiers 1-2 ignored the `state` arg
(callers `derive-council.ts:29` + `qld-globe.ts:295` DO pass it; only tier 3 honoured it), so a Canberra
address's Mapbox name substring-matched **"Gold Coast City Council"** (QLD) → `1 London Circuit,
Canberra ACT 2600` returned `lgaName="Gold Coast City Council"`. `.find()` returns the FIRST national
match, so the wrong state wins. FIX (deployed + on main `99d0c7e`): `inState = (l) => !state ||
l.state===state`, gate every fuzzy tier on it → an ACT lookup can only match an ACT LGA; worst case →
null → the boundary-GeoJSON point-in-polygon fallback (authoritative) or raw name — both safer than a
confident wrong-state LGA. **Principle:** any fuzzy/substring resolution against a national dataset, when
the jurisdiction is already known, MUST filter to that jurisdiction first — fuzzy match is a last resort
on an already-narrowed set, never the whole country. Corollary: prefer geographic (point-in-polygon)
resolution over name fuzzy-matching wherever a boundary dataset exists.

**Also confirmed 2026-07-05 (8-state live derive):** the engine returns real zoning + cadastre + overlays
across all 8 states for **normal residential addresses**; CBD/commercial parcels can return null zoning/lot
(hard parcels, not engine gaps). Universal layer (slope via Mapbox-DEM ~30m fallback / QLD LiDAR, wind,
climate, BAL) is genuinely 8/8. So "full suite" = full-coverage/mixed-fidelity for typical addresses, with
deliberate planner-by-design gaps (title/contamination/servicing/native-title), NOT "authoritative
everything everywhere."

name: org-merge-membership-guarantee
description: "Org-merge / org-delete migrations must guarantee canonical membership exists before re-anchoring, OR refuse + surface broken profiles for manual review. Silent NULL strands users."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 7a593fb5-3c82-4a67-abab-d344f95ee288

When writing any migration that deletes / merges / consolidates organisations,
the re-anchor step MUST either:
  (a) GUARANTEE the canonical membership row exists for every affected user
      BEFORE setting their `profile.active_organisation_id`, or
  (b) REFUSE to re-anchor those users + surface them via RAISE NOTICE for
      manual review.

Never silently set `active_organisation_id = NULL` for users who happen to
not have a canonical membership at apply time. Same applies to bulk
membership cleanup, org-archive flows, and the eventual "Lane C drops
the legacy organisation_id column" cutover.

**Why:** On 2026-05-21, migration 038 deleted a duplicate "Corporate AI
Solutions" org. The migration's UPDATE on profiles used `CASE WHEN
EXISTS(canonical membership) THEN canonical ELSE NULL`. The problem: the
doomed-org cascade had already deleted the user's old membership row
before the CASE check ran in the same statement, AND the canonical
membership turned out not to exist for dennis@corporateaisolutions.com
(despite him actively browsing the canonical org earlier the same day —
something cleared that membership between then and apply time). Result:
his profile got `active_organisation_id = NULL` with `memberships =
[]` → authenticated session but stranded outside any org → silent
`/dashboard` 404 on every sign-in attempt. Took two middleware patches
(neither of which could help, since there was no membership to fall
back to) plus a diagnostic migration 039 to pin down. The CASE-NULL
branch is the load-bearing failure mode — it looks defensive but it's
actually destructive.

**How to apply:**
- In any migration that DELETEs or merges orgs, write the membership
  upsert FIRST (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` for every affected
  user → canonical), THEN re-anchor profiles, THEN drop the doomed org.
- If you can't guarantee canonical membership (e.g. you don't know the
  right role to grant), don't NULL the column — instead leave the
  active_organisation_id pointing at the doomed UUID and RAISE NOTICE
  the affected user list so a human can adjudicate. A dangling UUID is
  recoverable (the middleware fallback can find another membership);
  a NULL with zero memberships is not.
- For the eventual Lane C drop of `profile.organisation_id` legacy
  column (per [[multi-org-legacy-column-audit]]), audit must include
  the same guarantee: every active user has at least one membership
  row before the column is dropped.
- Same DNA as [[clarify-over-fail]] — silent degradation strands the
  user; surface for human decision instead. Same DNA as
  [[atomic-migration-sequencing]] — order matters, and "looks
  defensive" is not the same as "is defensive."

⚠️ **Kira RENAMES the convai tables** via `KIRA_CONVAI_TABLES` (`lib/kira/convai.ts`). There is no
`convai_agents` / `convai_memory` — querying those returns "table not found" and reads as nothing

## The root cause — the part worth remembering

The earlier reading ("the tools were never added") was **wrong**. They *were* added:
`reprovisionBusinessAgentsForExec({apply:true})` had run, and the ElevenLabs workspace held 5 owners ×
a correct, uid-baked `dispatch_task`/`approve_task` pair. Every one was **orphaned — referenced by no

memory + knowledge. **`setAgentTools` REPLACES an agent's tool list**, so a tool omitted there is not
skipped, it is removed. The tool-secret migration (commit `81f37e7`, "migration complete") is a run of
that very script — closing one gap silently opened another. Two reprovision paths existed with
different tool sets, and the incomplete one ran last.

**The lesson generalises:** where an API call *replaces* a set rather than merging into it, any second
code path that builds that set is a regression waiting for its turn to run. `doing-tools-def.mjs` even

  currently-attached, working tool (compare hashes) before reusing it.

**Always `git checkout main` BEFORE `git checkout -b <new-branch>`.** Branching from whatever happens
to be checked out makes the new PR contain the *other* branch's commits too.

**Why:** on 2026-07-31 a docs branch was cut while sitting on `feat/signup-hubspot-capture`, so
**PR #137 ("docs only — a spec") actually contained PR #136's unapproved signup→HubSpot feature.**
Merging what read as a harmless spec would have shipped code that was explicitly being held for
Karen + Karthik sign-off, on a REGULATED client product — silently bypassing the exact gate #136's
own description existed to enforce. It was caught only because Dennis asked an unrelated question
about why the repo was sitting on a branch, which prompted a `git diff --stat main...HEAD`.

This repo makes it likelier than usual: the working tree is **shared across sessions**, so the
checked-out branch is often not the one you left, and `git branch --show-current` is already a
standing check here (see [[project_call_backlog_2026_06_25]]).

**How to apply:**
- Before `checkout -b`, confirm the base: `git branch --show-current` → `git checkout main`.
- After opening any PR, verify it contains only what you intend:
  `git log --oneline main..HEAD` and `gh pr view <n> --json changedFiles,commits`.
  A PR described as "docs only" that reports 6 changed files is the tell.
- Fix a wrong base with `git rebase --onto main <wrong-base> <branch>` then
  `git push --force-with-lease` — safe when the branch is new and unreviewed, and `--force-with-lease`
  refuses if anything changed underneath. Confirm with Dennis first: force-push is on the
  safety list.
- **Never describe a PR's scope from the commit you wrote — describe it from what the PR reports.**
  Saying "docs-only, safe to merge" about an unverified diff is how the gate gets bypassed.

A run that reports defects a five-minute script would have caught has been half wasted, and the
findings that matter get buried under them.
